conviction_note: The one fresh, company-level counterparty number is positive. Montage, Rambus's main DDR5 RCD rival, pre-announced on 2026-10-20 that Q3 interconnect-chip revenue rose 20.9% QoQ, against Rambus's guide of about +14% QoQ for product revenue, and said Q4 demand rises further. Against that, RMBS fell on each of its last four prints (-8.7, -13.4, -21.3, -9.0), including a Q2 beat above its guide range, and the 25d skew pays for downside (+3.17). The scaled number is therefore only slightly positive: p_up 53 on abs_move 12 gives +0.72, against an impact_sum of +1.1. The two numbers agree in sign; they differ because the sells-the-beat history sits in p_up rather than in the findings.
bar: Q3 revenue $213m: the company guide midpoint of $210-216m (product $110-116m, royalties $69-75m, contract and other $25-31m; non-GAAP EPS $0.75-0.82), from the Q2 release 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000917273/000119312526318063/rmbs-ex99_1.htm (2026-07-27). Two estimate sources agree: Yahoo shows 6 analysts averaging $213.02m (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/RMBS/analysis/) and Benzinga shows about $213m revenue and $0.76 EPS (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/rmbs/earnings). TipRanks shows $0.79 EPS. The Q4 revenue consensus is about $225-227m (Benzinga, one source showing two values, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/RMBS/earnings-forecasts), so the Q4 bar is softer. The guide release says reaching the range requires signing customer agreements for product sales and solutions licensing.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest at 2026-09-30 was 4,784,389 shares, 1.45 days to cover, down from 6,222,309 (3.22 days) at 2026-09-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/rmbs/shortinterest). That is about 4-5% of roughly 108m shares, so not a crowded short; Benzinga put it at 7.6% of float around 2026-09-24. Skew: 25d put minus call is +3.17 vol points, so downside is paid; put/call OI is 0.82. The event-implied move is 13.11% (straddle 18.09%) against a 7-print median reaction of 8.99%. Tape: -13.9% over 20 days, -5.1% over 5 days, -48.5% from the 52-week high and +10.3% off the low. October month-to-date was -17.7% per AAII on 2026-10-26, on a sector selloff with no company news. Insiders: a director (Kissner) made two 5,000-share sales under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-05-08, at $105 on 9/22 and $111 on 10/2.

findings.finding: Montage Technology, Rambus's largest competitor in DDR5 RCD and memory interface chips, pre-announced Q3 2026 on 2026-10-20. Interconnect-chip revenue was about RMB 2.047bn, +20.9% QoQ and +49.3% YoY, after about +20% QoQ in Q2. Interconnect gross margin was 68.0-68.5%, up 0.6-1.1 points QoQ. Management said Q4 interconnect demand will rise further, citing a rising mix of 3rd-5th generation RCD. Rambus guided Q3 product revenue to $110-116m, +14% QoQ at the midpoint off $99.2m. If the buffer-chip market grew about 20% QoQ in Q3 and Rambus held share, product revenue lands at or above the top of its guide ($116m), and a Q4 product guide up QoQ is more likely than the flat-to-down Q4 the Baird 'shortage caps units' thesis implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Product revenue has beaten repeatedly without being paid. Q2 2026 product revenue was $99.2m (+13% QoQ) and total revenue beat the top of guidance, yet the stock fell 8.99%; Q1 2026 was a solid beat and fell 21.26% on a downgrade about 2027 units. The last four prints fell -8.71, -13.42, -21.26 and -8.99 (baseline). What has moved the stock is the forward unit narrative, so this finding is filed on guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: RMBS fell 5.1% in the five sessions after Montage's pre-announcement and sits 10% above its 52-week low, with put skew bid. If the market had carried Montage's +21% QoQ and its Q4 demand comment over to Rambus, the stock would have rallied off the 10/20 print, not drifted down into its own. The pre-announcement was in Chinese and HK/Shanghai coverage, with no English Rambus preview citing it that I could find. Caveat: Montage's growth may include share gains at Rambus's expense, since Montage cites a rising share of new-generation RCD. Rambus's own guide already embeds +14% QoQ, so only the gap of roughly 6 points of product growth (about $6m, ~3% of revenue) is new.
findings.independence: Goldman (via caiwennews, 2026-10-21, https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1661330.shtml) reads the same Montage document: revenue in line with GS and 1% above Bloomberg consensus, net profit 30% above GS. That is the same document, so it is not independent. A different source pointing the same way is Micron's FQ4 (2026-09-30): server unit growth forecast in the high teens, https://pulse2.com/micron-reports-record-fiscal-q4-revenue-of-54-23-billion-and-fy2026-revenue-of-133-19-billion/

findings.finding: Server CPU demand, which drives RCD units, was very strong per direct customers of the ecosystem. Intel's Q2 2026 DCAI revenue rose 59% YoY to $6.3bn, with Xeon demand outrunning supply partly because of memory and substrate shortages (reported July 2026). Micron's FQ4 2026 (2026-09-30) forecast server units growing in the high teens and said over 75% of FY27 shipments are under allocation or contract. Both point to RCD unit demand above supply, not below it, in H2 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific. The market has repeatedly treated strong server demand as already priced for RMBS; Q2 'H2 stronger than H1' commentary still sold off 9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these are public macro prints from July and September. It is filed as a small proxy because it is macro-to-company transmission that Rambus itself has not confirmed. If it were unpriced, RMBS would not be 48% off its high while Micron reports records.
findings.independence: Intel Q2 2026 DCAI +59% YoY with demand ahead of supply, summarised in search coverage of Intel's July 2026 print. The Nasdaq article https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/intel-just-delivered-investors-here-are-6-key-things-know is from a different source than Micron. It shares the demand thesis with the Montage finding but rests on different documents.

findings.finding: The bear thesis on units is live and sourced. TrendForce (July 2026) projects RDIMM supply growing only 15-20% in 2027, well behind server CPU supply, implying an RDIMM shortage in 2027. Its July server DIMM report notes short-term inventory rising because processor shortages delay server assembly and buyers stockpile. Fusion Worldwide reports servers shipping with little or no memory installed. This is the Baird downgrade thesis of 2026-04-28 (RMBS cannot raise prices in a shortage, and units are capped), and it is what a 2027 or Q4 commentary could confirm.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line moved the stock -21.26% on 2026-04-28, when Baird cut to Neutral on 2027 RDIMM growth slowing from DRAM shortages (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/04/28/why-rambus-plunged-today/). In each of the last four prints the forward/2027 narrative dominated a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is the consensus bear case behind a stock 48% off its high and with put skew bid. What remains unpriced is whether management quantifies a 2027 RDIMM unit constraint on the call, which would be new. If it were fully priced, a strong Montage print would have lifted RMBS, and it did not.
findings.independence: Fusion Worldwide, RDIMM shortages blog, https://info.fusionww.com/blog/rdimm-shortages-and-the-shift-in-server-shipments (different source, same thesis). This partly contradicts finding 2. They are reconciled into one direction: demand above supply means Q3/Q4 revenue is supported, while 2027 unit growth is the risk.

findings.finding: RMBS went into the print down 17.7% month-to-date and down 13.9% over 20 days. The October declines (-6.0% on 10/12, -6.05% on 10/16) were attributed to a semiconductor and AI-infrastructure selloff with no company-specific news, and the 10/5 call-date notice carried no warning. This lowers the bar relative to the Q2 setup: Q2 came in after a run-up to about $96 and Q1 after a 72% YTD run.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 was sold -21% after a 72% YTD run-up. Q2 was sold -9% after a run toward $96, then rebounded about 21% in early August. This print is the first in 2026 to come in after a drawdown, not a run-up.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is itself the price, so this finding is about lower expectations, not new information. That is why it is sized small: a drawdown without a company cause is not evidence of over-reaction. Short interest is low (1.45 days to cover), so no squeeze mechanism is in play.

findings.finding: Rambus launched a $100m accelerated share repurchase with Mizuho on 2026-08-05, receiving about 796k shares upfront and due to complete by end of Q3 2026. Final settlement at the Q3 VWAP less a discount (shares traded $95-111 in Aug-Sep) should take the Q3 average diluted share count slightly below the 110m guide assumption. That is a small non-GAAP EPS tailwind, under 1%, and the release frames it as confidence ahead of H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; prior quarters carried only token buybacks ($2.96m in H1 2026 per 10-Q).
findings.why_not_priced: Public 8-K, so the amount is priced. Whether a follow-on authorization or ASR is announced with the print is not. If a further authorization were expected, it would show as support into the print, and the stock has instead fallen 18% in October.
findings.independence: The 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000917273/000119312526321000/rmbs-20260630.htm) shows $824.9m cash and securities at 6/30, so capacity exists. Same company, different document.

findings.finding: Q3 royalties are guided down to $69-75m from $84.2m in Q2 (licensing billings $84.1m). MRDIMM revenue is guided 'minimal' in Q4 and 'material in 2027'. Both are inside what the company already guided, so a print in line on these lines is expected.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Royalty swings come from ASC 606 timing on license renewals and have not driven the recent reactions; the forward product narrative has.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: this is the company's own guide. It is filed so the panel sees that the Q2-to-Q3 royalty step-down is expected, not a miss.
findings.independence: Same company release; the 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000917273/000119312526318063/rmbs-ex99_1.htm is the same document.

findings.finding: Finance leadership has turned over: CFO Lynch resigned in February, Sumeet Gagneja (ex-AMD Data Center divisional CFO) became CFO on 2026-04-29, and Chief Accounting Officer John Allen retired effective 2026-09-08, three weeks before quarter-end. William Taulbee, a VP Accounting hired in August 2026, replaced him; the 8-K states no disagreement. This is the second guide set by a new CFO.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measurable. Q2 was the first print under Gagneja and fell 9% on an in-line guide (Quiver attributed it to the guide being merely in line).
findings.why_not_priced: Public 8-K, ignored by coverage. The only mechanism is a conservative guide style from a new CFO, which is speculative, hence the small size.

findings.finding: Rambus's own inventory rose 70% to $74.8m at 2026-06-30 from $44.1m at 2025-12-31. Management called it a strategic build for anticipated demand and said it had seen no customer inventory accumulation. TrendForce's July note says buyers were stockpiling and short-term inventory was rising because processor shortages delayed server assembly. If module makers are stocked ahead of delayed server builds, Q4 RCD orders could pause.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific; inventory has not been a headline line in prior reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The build is in the 10-Q and rarely discussed. A channel stockpiling read would show as Q4 product guide flat or down, and a Q4 consensus of about $225m assumes growth. Montage's 'Q4 demand rises further' argues against a pause, which is why this is small.
findings.independence: TrendForce Server DIMM Price Jul. 2026, https://www.trendforce.com/research/download/RP260731NW (different source on channel stockpiling). Montage's Q4 comment (finding 1) cuts against it.

outside_window.finding: MRDIMM and 16-channel next-generation CPU platform revenue are guided as material only in 2027, so any upside there is beyond this print's window except as commentary.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly long, which cuts against the +3.17 put skew and the four straight post-print declines. The 20-day run-up of -13.9% and the 18% October drawdown agree with a lower bar, so the evidence partly agrees with the run-up and disagrees with the skew. p_up is held at 53 for that reason.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Montage read-through is cut from +2.0 to +1.5, because RMBS sold its last four prints, including a Q2 beat above its guide; p_up goes from 54 to 53.

Lesson 5 (the absence of a cause is not evidence): the October-drawdown positioning finding is cut from +1.0 to +0.3, because 'down without company news, so the bar is lower' is the pattern the file warns against.

Lesson 5 (proxy vs broad series): the 2027 RDIMM shortage thesis is a public industry proxy already behind the -48% drawdown, so it is cut from -1.5 to -1.0. The Intel/Micron demand proxy is left at +0.5.
Lesson 4/rejected candidates: the director 10b5-1 sales (a separate draft finding at 0.0) are moved into positioning_check and rejected_candidates, which takes the count from 9 to 8.
Lessons 6 and 7 left standing: the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources, short interest is checked and not crowded, and MRDIMM 2027 is moved to outside_window.
